source: Introduction through a founder in your Fund I portfolio.
benchmark_status: provisional: Phase 3 sets it from the backtest and evals

criteria.why: Both founders are full-time, and the CEO has 8 years in FMCG distribution and field operations, which is the exact problem. The CTO built the app and credit rules. Neither has startup experience, and there is no evidence yet of selling or building beyond the pilot. LinkedIn and background are not verified.

claims.quote: 8 years in FMCG distribution and field operations

rules: capped: a fact could not be found outside the deck

criteria.why: The channel is working at small scale (field agents brought in 24 of 38 stores), and CAC and payback are stated with their method. But the sample is one town and the October CAC is INR 2,860, against a form claim of under INR 2,000. Payback is about 5.5 months. There is no named first buyer, and the agent-free route is untested.

criteria.why: Repeat use is reported (22 of 42 ordered more than once), which is better than sign-ups alone. But the deck and form disagree on retailer count, CAC and credit funding. GMV is given for different periods: INR 3.8 L in October against about INR 9 L over three months. None of it is checkable.

claims.quote: 42 retailers onboarded, 22 of whom have ordered more than once

criteria.why: There is little that compounds yet. The credit-scoring approach is claimed as an edge but not shown. The local-language app and small-town focus can be copied. Possible data and distribution advantages are early, and there is a regulatory gap because it is not an NBFC.

claims.text: Founders say credit scoring is an edge, without showing it
claims.quote: We have been told our credit-scoring approach is an edge.

missing.item: Evidence that the credit-scoring model outperforms alternatives

criteria.why: A B2B restocking marketplace with embedded credit for kirana stores is closer to fintech and commerce enablement than the Consumer tech label. It sits inside the fund's sectors.

claims.text: Restocking app with short-term credit for kirana stores
claims.quote: B2B restocking app with short-term credit for small-town kirana stores.

criteria.why: INR 2 Cr is roughly USD 240K, at or just below the fund's cheque range, and the use of funds is tied to 300 stores and INR 40 L GMV. The INR 12 Cr post-money valuation looks rich against about INR 3.8 L monthly GMV. The credit book takes 40% of the funds, and the funding of credit is unclear.
